manuscript_title: Double-bond geometry determines fatty acid metabolic fate and ferroptosis sensitivity

required_revisions.text: Mechanistic: SCD-dependent conversion of petroselaidic acid — Add WT + doxycycline control to Figure 3E; perform SCD CRISPR knockout + rescue with catalytically dead SCD to distinguish catalytic vs. off-target effects; include these data in revised Figure 3 or new supplementary figure.

Mechanistic: Structural identity of trans-18:2 metabolite — Perform LC-MS/MS with authentic 6E,9Z-linopetroselaidic acid standard (synthesized or purchased) to confirm metabolite identity by retention time and MS/MS fragmentation; if standard unavailable, use ozone-induced dissociation (OzID) or NMR on purified metabolite to assign double-bond geometry/position; include structural validation data in revised manuscript.

Mechanistic: Phospholipid remodeling convergence — Qualify all remodeling claims as 'correlative' in Abstract, Results, Discussion, Figure 7, and title; add perturbation experiments (e.g., ACSL4 KO, LPCAT3 KD, MBOAT1/2 KD) testing necessity of diPUFA/sn-1 incorporation (linoelaidic) and arachidonate enrichment (petroselaidic) for ferroptosis sensitization; if not feasible in revision, explicitly state these are future directions and temper causal language throughout.

Statistical rigor: Add biological replicate numbers (n) and replicate type (biological vs technical) to all figure legends; specify exact statistical test for each comparison (e.g., 'two-way ANOVA with Dunnett's post-hoc test, n=4'); define error bars as SEM or SD in each legend; add FDR correction for lipidomics species comparisons (Benjamini-Hochberg, q<0.05); include equivalence test or confidence intervals for Figure 3D 'rescue to control levels' claim; report FALCON screen hit-calling criteria, replicate numbers, statistical thresholds, and multiple-testing correction.

Data deposition: Deposit raw and processed lipidomics data (LC-MS/MS MRM files, shotgun lipidomics peak tables) to MetaboLights; deposit GC-FID chromatograms and OmegaQuant protocol details to Figshare; deposit FALCON screen raw Incucyte images and normalization script to GitHub/Zenodo; add data availability statement with accessions.

Methods completeness (HARD gaps from audit): Report sample size (n) and replicate type for every experiment (FALCON screen, dose-response, GC-FID, immunoblots, flow cytometry, LC-MS/MS, targeted lipidomics); provide RRIDs for all primary and secondary antibodies, explicitly state host species and clonality; provide RRID/CVCL identifiers and STR authentication records for all cell lines (including elephant seal primary endothelial cells); provide plasmid source (Addgene #), construct description (promoter, tag, selection marker), and validation details for mCherry-NLS and Tet-on SCD overexpression lines; deposit mass spectrometry data to public repository (MassIVE/PRIDE) and provide accession; report objective NA for confocal, detector settings for Incucyte and confocal, software versions for Incucyte and Harmony, and full gating strategy for flow cytometry.

Citation integrity: Verify accessibility of future-year references (Refs 14, 27, 42) — replace with accessible preprints or published versions if available; complete missing page/article numbers for Refs 26, 32, 36, 46, 48, 49, 50, 53, 55; verify that Refs 47–51 directly support the cited claims and adjust citations if needed.

Clarity fixes per author concessions: Correct Figure 3A caption to accurately reflect time-course data (0, 4, 8, 24 hr) and fix duplicated lipid species label to 'trans 18:1, cis 18:2, and trans 18:2'; revise Abstract petroselinic acid statement to reflect Figure 2G data (protection only with FSP1 inhibition); qualify all sn-1 positional claims as 'inferred from acyl chain composition' in Results, Figure 6 legend, Figure 7, and Discussion; add explicit Methods statement that Lipidyzer shotgun lipidomics does not resolve sn-positional isomers.

minor_suggestions: Expand targeted oxidized phospholipid analysis to PE and PI classes in future work to comprehensively assess stereochemical oxidation signatures.
Consider isotope tracing (e.g., 13C-labeled fatty acids) for flux quantification of metabolic conversion pathways in follow-up studies.
Disclose the approximate self-citation count (9 of 55 references from Olzmann group/collaborators) in a transparency statement.

If perturbation experiments for phospholipid remodeling are not feasible in this revision, clearly label the correlative lipidomics data as hypothesis-generating and specify the exact experiments needed for causal testing in the Discussion.

weaknesses.text: Figure 3A caption states "at time t = 0 hr" but the text describes "prolonged incubation" and the panel appears to show a time course; it also lists "trans 18:1, 18:2, and trans 18:2" with "trans 18:2" duplicated, making the actual measurements and timeline unrecoverable. This directly obscures the metabolic tracing evidence for SCD-dependent conversion of petroselaidic acid.

The results claim quantification of "phospholipids containing 18:2 at the sn-1 position" by shotgun lipidomics (Lipidyzer), but the Methods do not describe sn-positional resolution for this platform, leaving a central structural assignment unsubstantiated.

The abstract states petroselinic acid "suppressed ferroptosis," but the results show it only exhibited protection when FSP1 was pharmacologically inhibited (Figure 2G), overstating the baseline finding and misrepresenting the cis/trans comparison.

Quantitative claims throughout the Results use vague qualifiers ("substantially greater," "markedly increased," "pronounced leftward shift\)) without reporting fold-changes or effect sizes in the main text, forcing readers to infer magnitude from figures.

The FALCON screen used 1 mM free fatty acid — a supraphysiological concentration — without justification or discussion of physiological relevance, limiting interpretation of the screen's hit selection.
Figure 2E caption describes "dose responses" for cell death inhibitors but lists only single concentrations, creating confusion about what the panel displays.
The FALCON acronym expansion uses non-standard capitalization ("ONtologies\)) that may distract readers.

questions: What time points does Figure 3A actually represent, and can the caption be corrected to match both the data and the text's description of prolonged incubation?
Does the Lipidyzer shotgun lipidomics platform resolve sn-positional isomers, and if so, is this documented in the cited method or a supplementary protocol?
Were the commercial trans fatty acid preparations (linoelaidic acid, petroselaidic acid) verified for purity and absence of cis isomers that could confound the stereochemistry-specific effects?

weaknesses.text: Load-bearing claim 1 (trans fatty acids are potent ferroptosis sensitizers): The FALCON screen (Fig 1B) ranks hits by normalized AUC but does not state the number of biological replicates, the statistical test used to call 'hits', or any multiple-testing correction across 62 fatty acids × 2 cell lines × 2 conditions (±RSL3). Without this, the false-discovery rate for the top hits (linoelaidic, petroselaidic) is unknown. The text says 'reproducibly enhanced' but no replication number or variance is given for the screen itself.

Load-bearing claim 2 (petroselaidic acid requires SCD for ferroptosis sensitization): Figure 3D shows lethal fraction over time with and without CAY10566, but the figure legend and methods do not state n, the test comparing curves, or whether the comparison is at a single time point or AUC. The claim that SCD inhibition 'abolished the ability... reducing cell death to levels observed in control cells' is a quantitative equivalence claim that requires a powered equivalence test or at least a confidence interval for the difference; none is provided.

Load-bearing claim 3 (trans fatty acids remodel phospholipids to generate distinct ferroptosis-susceptible species): Figures 6C–I present lipidomics data with log2 fold-changes but no statistical test, n, or correction for the dozens of phospholipid species compared. The statement 'significantly increased' (e.g., diPUFA phospholipids in 6E) has no associated p-value or FDR. The methods mention 'normalized to cell count' but not how variability across replicates was handled.

Sweep: Figure 2A–D dose-response curves lack n and error-bar definitions in the legends; the methods say 'error bars in dose-response plots represent SEM' but do not state n for each curve. Figure 2E uses 'strongly suppressed' without a statistical comparison across five inhibitors. Figure 4B, C quantify lipid droplets and flow cytometry but do not report the test used for the multiple comparisons (Dunnett's is mentioned in methods for lipid droplets but not for flow cytometry). Figure 5A, B, D, E show median ratios or intensities with error bars but no n or test for the pairwise comparisons implied by the bars. The methods state 'ordinary one-way ANOVA and Dunnett's multiple comparisons test or Brown-Forsythe and Welch ANOVA tests with Dunnett's T3' but do not specify which test was used for which figure, and n is absent from all figure legends.

Sweep: The GC-FID fatty acid profiling (Fig 3A, 6A, Supp Fig 4A, B, E, F) reports absolute quantification but never states the number of biological replicates; 'normalized to cell count' is described but the unit of replication (independent culture dishes? independent passages?) is not defined.

Sweep: The SCD overexpression experiment (Fig 3E, Supp Fig 4I) shows lethal fraction over time for WT vs +dox but provides no n, no test for curve separation, and no verification that doxycycline alone has no effect (the WT + dox condition is missing).

Sweep: Several 'no difference' claims are made from non-significant results without power justification (e.g., 'FADS2 inhibition had no effect on RSL3 dose response' in Supp Fig 4C; 'DGAT1/2 inhibition failed to block ferroptosis sensitization' in Fig 4D–H and Supp Fig 5E–H).

Sweep: The Liperfluo and BODIPY C11 flow cytometry data (Fig 5A, B) present median fluorescence ratios but the gating strategy, number of cells analyzed per replicate, and number of replicates are not stated.

questions: For the FALCON screen (Fig 1B): How many biological replicates were performed per fatty acid per cell line? What statistical threshold (e.g., FDR, p-value) was used to define 'hits'?
For Figure 3D: What is n for each condition? Was the comparison between petroselaidic acid ± CAY10566 done at a single time point or on AUC? What test was used?
For Figures 6C–I: What is n for the lipidomics? What statistical test and multiple-testing correction were applied to the phospholipid species comparisons?
For Figure 2E: What test was used to compare cell death across the five inhibitors? What is n?
For the GC-FID data (Fig 3A, 6A, Supp Fig 4): What is the unit of replication and n for each fatty acid treatment?
For Figure 3E: What is n? Was a WT + doxycycline control included? What test compared the curves?
For the flow cytometry lipid peroxidation assays (Fig 5A, B): How many cells were analyzed per replicate? How many biological replicates? What test compared median ratios?

weaknesses.text: The 2025 Cancer Research paper by Park et al. cited for MUFA suppression of ferroptosis could not be independently verified from abstract alone; authors should confirm it supports the specific claim.
The 2026 reference to Joseph in 'Ferroptosis and Oxidative Stress' journal should be verified for publication status and relevance to FINO2/FIN56 mechanisms.
The citation of Harayama 2023 (Biochimie review) for 'understanding remains incomplete' is appropriate but a primary research gap statement might be stronger.
The FALCON screen method citation (Wieder 2023) is used for a different biological question (ferroptosis vs lipotoxicity); this is fine but could be clarified in the text.

questions: Does the Park et al. 2025 Cancer Research paper directly demonstrate cis MUFA suppression of ferroptosis, or is it a correlative lipid composition study?
Is the Joseph 2026 reference a published paper or a preprint, and does it specifically address FINO2/FIN56 mechanisms as cited?

weaknesses.text: The claim that SCD directly desaturates petroselaidic acid to a trans/cis-18:2 PUFA lacks direct biochemical evidence: no in vitro assay with purified SCD and petroselaidyl-CoA, and GC-FID identifies only a 'trans 18:2' peak without structural confirmation (e.g., MS/MS or NMR) that it is 6E,9Z-18:2. SCD inhibition globally depletes MUFAs and independently promotes ferroptosis, confounding the rescue interpretation.

Phospholipid remodeling is presented as the mechanistic convergence point but remains correlative. No genetic or pharmacological perturbation of the specific remodeling pathways (e.g., ACSL4, LPCAT3, MBOAT1/2 for sn-1 incorporation or diPUFA generation) tests whether these changes are necessary for the ferroptosis sensitization by either trans fatty acid.

The primary FALCON screen tests only two cancer cell lines (H460, U-2 OS) with a single GPX4 inhibitor (RSL3) at one timepoint. Hits are not validated in the screen against non-ferroptotic death or in non-cancer models, risking false positives from cell-line-specific metabolism or off-target toxicity at 1 mM fatty acid.

Metabolic tracing uses endpoint GC-FID at limited timepoints without isotope tracing or flux analysis, so the relative contributions of direct incorporation vs. elongation/desaturation vs. remodeling cannot be quantified. The claim that linoleic acid does not convert to arachidonic acid in 24h is based on a single timepoint in one cell line.

Targeted oxidized phospholipid analysis is restricted to PC species with available synthetic standards, omitting PE, PI, and other classes known to be ferroptosis-relevant. The authors acknowledge this limitation but the conclusion that linoelaidic acid generates 'unique oxidation products' is overstated given the narrow analytical window.

questions: Was the 'trans 18:2' metabolite from petroselaidic acid structurally confirmed as 6E,9Z-18:2 (linopetroselaidic acid) by MS/MS or NMR, or is the assignment based solely on SCD's known Δ9 regioselectivity?

In the SCD inhibition rescue (Fig 3D), SCD inhibitor alone increases RSL3 killing (Suppl Fig S4G,H). The combination of SCD inhibitor + petroselaidic acid returns death to BSA control levels — is this interpreted as petroselaidic acid's effect being blocked, or as two opposing effects canceling? How was this distinction made?
For the lipidomics (Fig 6), were the sn-1/sn-2 assignments inferred from acyl chain composition or determined by positional analysis (e.g., phospholipase digestion)?

weaknesses.text: The targeted oxidized phospholipid analysis (Figure 5) captures only a defined subset of phosphatidylcholine hydroperoxides for which standards existed; the authors acknowledge that petroselaidic acid's robust ferroptosis sensitization is not fully reflected in these data, leaving the specific oxidized species driving its activity incompletely defined. This gap means the mechanistic link between petroselaidic acid's metabolic conversion and the actual peroxidation substrates remains partially inferential.

Cell-line variability in the DGAT inhibition experiments (Figure 4, Supplementary Figure S5) is noted but not mechanistically explored; U-2 OS cells show qualitatively different responses to DGAT inhibition under petroselaidic acid treatment compared to H460 cells, and the manuscript does not explain whether this reflects differential lipid handling, baseline ferroptosis sensitivity, or off-target effects of the inhibitors.

The claim that trans-fatty acids do not promote ferroptosis through intrinsic oxidizability (Discussion) relies on literature showing trans-PUFAs oxidize slower than cis-PUFAs in vitro, but the manuscript does not directly measure oxidation kinetics of the relevant phospholipid species in cells, leaving a small but non-trivial gap between the cited biophysical data and the cellular context.

questions: Could the authors clarify whether the trans-18:2 metabolite generated from petroselaidic acid (putatively linopetroselaidic acid, 6E,9Z-18:2) was definitively identified by mass spectrometry or retention time matching, or is its structure inferred from the SCD-dependence and known SCD regioselectivity?

In the lipidomics data (Figure 6H,I), several phospholipids increased by petroselaidic acid are consistent with 18:1/20:4 species; were any of these confirmed to contain the trans-18:1 (petroselaidic) versus the SCD-generated trans/cis-18:2 at the sn-1 position, and does this distinction affect interpretation of which metabolite drives phospholipid remodeling?

The manuscript states that FADS2 inhibition had no effect on ferroptosis sensitization by any fatty acid (Supplementary Figure S4C); given that FADS2 is the Δ6-desaturase and petroselaidic acid already has a Δ6-trans bond, this is expected, but was FADS1 (Δ5-desaturase) or elongation activity assessed to rule out further metabolism of the SCD-generated trans/cis-18:2 to longer-chain trans-PUFAs?

weaknesses.text: The central lipidomics evidence (Figures 5, 6, Supplementary Figures 4, 5) relies on data processed through an "in-house platform" at the UCLA Lipidomics Core with no deposition of raw files, peak tables, or processing code; without these, the phospholipid remodeling and hydroperoxide isomer quantifications cannot be verified or re-analyzed.

The FALCON screen (Figure 1) references a prior publication (Wieder et al., 2023) for library preparation and screening protocol but does not confirm identical cell seeding densities, fatty acid conjugation batches, or Incucyte analysis parameters; the screening AUC normalization method is described in prose but not codified, so the hit list cannot be computationally reproduced.

GC-FID fatty acid profiling (Figures 3, 6, Supplementary Figure 4) was performed at OmegaQuant with an "internal protocol" — no method details (derivatization, column, temperature program) or raw chromatograms are provided, making the trans-18:2 metabolite identification and quantification unverifiable.

No data availability statement appears in the manuscript; neither raw nor processed datasets are deposited in a public repository (MetaboLights, PRIDE, GEO, Figshare, etc.), and "available on reasonable request" is not offered, so all load-bearing empirical data are inaccessible.

Custom analysis pipelines for dose-response curves (AUC, lethal fraction), lipid droplet image quantification (Harmony software pipeline), and flow cytometry gating are not shared as code or versioned workflows, preventing exact replication of the quantitative outputs in Figures 1, 2, 4, 5.

questions: Where are the raw and processed lipidomics datasets (LC-MS/MS hydroperoxide MRM data, shotgun lipidomics peak tables) deposited, and what is the accession/DOI?
Is the "in-house platform" used for lipidomics data processing at UCLA available as versioned code (GitHub/Zenodo) or a container image?
Can the FALCON screen raw Incucyte images and per-well lethal fraction time courses be provided, along with the exact normalization script used to compute AUC values?
Are the GC-FID raw chromatograms and OmegaQuant's internal protocol (derivatization, column, gradient) available for the fatty acid profiling data?
What are the exact Harmony high-content analysis pipeline settings (segmentation thresholds, spot detection parameters) used for lipid droplet quantification in Figure 4?

weaknesses.text: The claim that double-bond geometry 'determines' metabolic fate is mechanistically complete only for petroselaidic acid (SCD-dependent Δ9 desaturation); for linoelaidic acid, the paper shows preferential incorporation into diPUFA phospholipids and sn-1 18:2 species but does not identify the enzymatic machinery responsible, leaving 'determines' as a descriptive correlation rather than a demonstrated mechanism.

sn-position assignments and exact molecular species (e.g., petroselaidic acid at sn-1 paired with arachidonate at sn-2) are inferred from shotgun lipidomics without chiral or positional standards; the authors acknowledge this limitation, but the abstract and model figure present these architectures as established facts.

The generalization that 'fatty acid double-bond geometry determines ferroptosis sensitivity' rests on two C18 cis/trans pairs and three mixed isomers tested in a 62-compound screen across a handful of cancer lines; the title and abstract present this as a broad principle without qualifying the structural and cellular scope actually tested.

questions: For linoelaidic acid, which acyltransferases or remodeling enzymes mediate the preferential sn-1 incorporation and diPUFA phospholipid formation?
Can the trans-18:2 metabolite from petroselaidic acid be structurally confirmed as 6E,9Z-linopetroselaidic acid (vs. other trans-18:2 isomers) using authentic standards?
Do the ferroptosis-sensitizing effects of trans fatty acids persist at physiologically relevant concentrations (e.g., ≤10 μM) rather than the 100–200 μM used here?
